package_info.package_name: azureazure, azure-sdk-v4, glints-sdk, azure-sdk-v3, azurefilter, azure-filter-2, jetpack-api, jetpack-connection, labrujha-cadas, jetpack-components, jetpack-config, grunt-jsdoc-to-markdow, other-item, react-instantsearch-hooks-dom, string_decoder-browserify, parcel-plugin-test
package_info.why_malicious: These packages perform dependency confusion attacks, exfiltrate sensitive system and user information to attacker-controlled endpoints using legitimate SaaS webhook services, and sometimes use obfuscation or DNS tunneling to evade detection. The behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and is designed to steal data from victim environments.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or postinstall, the code collects system information (username, hostname, home directory, DNS servers, external IP, directory listing) and sends it via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml, enabling exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating system and user information to an external, attacker-controlled domain is a hallmark of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect or transmit host/user information to unknown endpoints during install or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting (with user consent and clear documentation).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or postinstall, obfuscated code performs the same data collection and exfiltration as snippet_1, but uses code obfuscation to evade static analysis and detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent and evade detection, especially when combined with network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely obfuscate install-time code, especially for basic operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation for intellectual property protection (rare for install scripts).
key_indicators: Mirrors behavior of known malicious code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code collects system and user information, exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml, and also encodes data into a DNS query for exfiltration via DNS tunneling.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dual exfiltration via HTTPS and DNS tunneling is highly suspicious and designed to evade network controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate install scripts do not exfiltrate host/user data or use DNS tunneling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None for DNS tunneling; telemetry via HTTPS only with user consent.
key_indicators: Custom install command with network activity

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed via dependency confusion (npm or PyPI).
Install/import-time code executes, collecting sensitive system and user information.
Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints via HTTPS POST and/or DNS tunneling.

behavioral_signatures: Install/import-time network requests to external domains
Collection of system/user/host information in install scripts
Obfuscated code in install or main entry points
DNS queries with encoded host/user data (DNS tunneling)
file_indicators: setup.py with CustomInstall class and network/DNS code
Obfuscated JavaScript in main entry point
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for install/import-time scripts in npm and PyPI packages that collect and transmit system/user information to external domains, especially those using known webhook or C2 services. Flag obfuscated code in install scripts and detect DNS queries with encoded data patterns. Correlate package names and versions with known IOCs and block or alert on suspicious network destinations.
